_comment: Freeze-proof system-protection policy — single source of truth, consumed by BOTH configuration_system-protection.nix (builtins.fromJSON, boot-time enforcement) AND build.sh (_apply_daemon_caps, live enforcement before every nix build). Hardware: Surface Pro 8, 8 logical CPUs, 8GB RAM, NVMe (none scheduler), zram swap + disk hibernate swapfile. The machine froze 10x because nix builds (running inside nix-daemon, NOT the client) ballooned RAM and thrashed pages to the disk swapfile. The fix layers: (1) nix-daemon hard-capped with MemorySwapMax=0 so a runaway build OOM-kills a compile job instead of swap-thrashing; (2) the GUI session gets guaranteed unreclaimable RAM; (3) an UNTOUCHABLE ISLAND (reserved RAM + realtime CPU + realtime IO) hosts the killers (freeze-guard, plus the now-disabled earlyoom) and the mesh (sshd/rescue) so they can ALWAYS act even when everything else is starved; (4) 2026-07-03 user directive 'ONLY PSI, remove ALL non-PSI triggers' — systemd-oomd (memory PSI) + freeze-guard (mem/io/cpu PSI active killer) are the ONLY two active killers; earlyoom (absolute mem%/swap%, zero PSI awareness) is disabled (sysprot.earlyoom.enable=false), kept data-driven so it can be re-enabled later if ever wanted.

no_hard_memcap_services._comment: Registry only — NOT read by any .nix consumer, exists so 'which services are deliberately left without a per-unit MemoryMax/MemoryHigh' is answerable by reading ONE file instead of grepping the whole repo. Continues the 2026-07-03 directive above ('ONLY PSI, remove ALL non-PSI triggers'). Every entry here previously had a hard memcg cap that was removed 2026-08-07 because it competed with/bypassed the global PSI watchdog (freeze-guard + systemd-oomd) as an independent kill path — plasmashell's own cap alone caused two freeze/crash incidents via memory.high throttle-thrash while real PSI stayed low. Add an entry here whenever you remove a per-service cap elsewhere, so the list stays the single place to check.
no_hard_memcap_services.wireguard-wstunnel client: ba_flakes_desktop/src/modules/wireguard-wstunnel.nix (connectivity-critical — CPUQuota throttle kept, memory kill removed)

specs._comment: U1 (PLAN-hardening-2026-07-07 §1C): desktop hardware specs, mirroring the vm-pilot schema _cloud-data-consolidated.json[._home_manager.vms.<vm>.specs] (ram_gb, cpu) so configuration_system-protection.nix derives its slice budgets from data instead of the old hardcoded cpus=8/ramMB=8192 let-bindings. The desktop is NOT in the cloud consolidated JSON (it is not a VM); this local desktop data file is its SoT. ram_gb×1024 = ramMB; cpu = logical CPUs (4 cores × 2 threads on the Surface Pro 8).

switch_isolation._comment: 2026-07-10 v3.1 — the deploy itself must never freeze the box. Every heavy `build.sh switch`/`pull` (6GB closure download + nix-store import) re-execs into workload.slice (a SYSTEM slice, sibling of user.slice — NOT under the desktop's user-1000.slice) bounded by memory_max/swap_max. So the transfer's memory counts against workload.slice, capped; if it balloons the kernel OOM-kills the SWITCH there and the compositor is untouched. This is why the box froze 5× on 2026-07-10: the switch ran in the desktop's own app.slice and its pressure thrashed the compositor. Guard env SWITCH_ISOLATED=1 stops infinite re-exec.

konsole_wrap._comment: 2026-07-18/19 — every interactive switch/pull MUST show visible, live progress: Diego was repeatedly blindsided by build.sh running headless with no popup/progress bar/terminal he could see (multiple incidents same day). Declarative, automatic, engine-level fix (not an ad-hoc manual konsole wrap): the FIRST time an interactive command runs and a desktop session is present, build.sh self-relaunches itself inside `konsole --hold` so there is ALWAYS a visible terminal streaming real output, PLUS a notify-send alert AND a kdialog progress bar fire immediately (three requirements, one data-driven block). Guarded by BUILD_SH_KONSOLE_WRAPPED=1 to stop infinite re-exec (same pattern as SWITCH_ISOLATED). Never fires in CI (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true) or when no desktop session is present (DISPLAY/DBUS unset) — falls through to plain execution. 2026-07-19 BUG FIX: the original exec used bare "$0" with no --workdir; konsole -e resolves relative paths against ITS OWN default cwd (not the caller's), so a relative invocation (./build.sh) died instantly inside konsole with zero output — looked like a hang, was actually a crash on line 1 of the re-exec. Fixed by resolving to $SCRIPT_DIR/build.sh + passing --workdir explicitly.

_rescue_port_comment: U1: Dropbear rescue-SSH port, mirroring vm-pilot's _cloud-data-consolidated.json[._home_manager.vms.<vm>.rescue_port]. Reachable only via wg0 (configuration_network.nix declares wg0 trusted).

nix_daemon._comment: Hard caps on nix-daemon.service — the ACTUAL build worker (cc1plus/rustc/ld run as its cgroup children). MemorySwapMax=0 = the build subtree can NEVER swap (not zram, not the disk swapfile) → the kernel OOM-kills one compile job instead of thrashing the disk → the desktop never freezes. cgroup v2 memory.max on the parent caps the whole subtree. Applied LIVE before every build by build.sh because 'nixos-rebuild switch' reloads unit files but does NOT re-apply resource control to the already-running daemon (this drift left the live daemon at 6G/4G-swap and caused the freezes).

gui_session._comment: user-1000.slice (the KDE Plasma desktop). MemoryMin = RAM the kernel is FORBIDDEN to reclaim, so the compositor (kwin/plasmashell) stays responsive under build pressure. 2026-07-02 FIX: MemorySwapMax=0 also blocked ZRAM (cgroup swap caps can't distinguish zram from disk) — with MemoryHigh below the real working set the kernel could only evict file-backed pages (running executables), which faulted straight back through kcryptd/btrfs = the freeze. 2026-07-03: valve 2G→6G — the 2G valve saturated (Redroid + multi-claude workload), reclaim had nowhere to spill while 17G of zram sat FREE, MemAvailable collapsed to 2% and earlyoom killed sessions/imports at near-zero PSI. 6G still lands zram-first (prio 100 vs disk -1); the disk swapfile is touched only after ~7.6G compressed zram truly fills.
gui_session._memoryhigh_note: 2026-07-10 v3 FIX: MemoryHigh 4505M→5400M. The 4505/5734 gap was a 1.2G 'throttle purgatory' — the 13:06 double-freeze was user-1000.slice hitting memory.high 1,146,211 times (memory.events high, oom_kill=0), doing endless direct reclaim (io.pressure full=62% for minutes) instead of ever killing. Narrowing the band to ~330M means memory.high is a brief ramp, not a permanent stall; escalation to a kill (oomd 30% / freeze-guard thrash voter) happens in seconds instead of never.

prochot_guard._comment: 2026-07-11 — the 200MHz incident. The Surface EC falsely asserted BD_PROCHOT (MSR 0x1FC bit0 read 1, re-latched after clearing) clamping ALL cores to 200MHz at 40°C (zero thermal-throttle events, correct governor). INVISIBLE to every existing monitor: PSI measures stalls not clock speed, so a 20x-slowed CPU reads as 'busy but healthy' (cpu full=0, load 10+). This guard is the missing KPI class: every interval_sec compare scaling_cur_freq against scaling_min_freq; sustained below the software floor is impossible except under a hardware clamp → journal CRIT + notify-send telling the user the EC needs a power-drain (hold power 30s, unplugged). Best-effort MSR bit0 clear is attempted (works when the assertion is transient, not when the EC re-latches). Consumed by configuration_system-protection.nix (prochot-guard.service + timer).

oom_hotkey._comment: 2026-07-16 — a physical escape hatch: hold RIGHTCTRL for hold_ms with no release → write sysrq_char to /proc/sysrq-trigger, which invokes the OOM killer IN KERNEL CONTEXT (same path as Alt+SysRq+F), so the kill can't get stuck behind busy/starved userspace. Implemented as a PASSIVE evdev watcher (oom-hotkey.py) — it OBSERVES /dev/input without grabbing, so RIGHTCTRL keeps working normally for everything (no latency, no modifier breakage) and a quick chord (RCtrl+C) never fires (keyup cancels the timer before hold_ms). The kernel input layer delivers key events even when the compositor is wedged, and the service runs in the untouchable island (connectivity.slice: realtime CPU/IO, MemoryMin, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000) so it always gets scheduled. Requires kernel.sysrq bit 64 (mask 244, already set) for the 'f' trigger to be honored. RIGHTCTRL chosen over ESC to avoid adding any latency to the vim/terminal-critical Esc key.

compositor_no_swap._comment: 2026-07-11 — 'the compositor can never be swapped'. Observed live: plasmashell had 238MB paged to swap, kwin 64MB, Xwayland 31MB; every click faulted them back from the NVMe = 5s GUI lag with PSI near 0 (single-process swap-in latency does not move the PSI averages). Linux NEVER proactively pulls swapped pages back — they return only when faulted on access — so once the compositor is out, it stays laggy until forced back. FIX: MemorySwapMax=0 on the COMPOSITOR USER UNITS ONLY (not the whole user-1000.slice — that whole-slice swap=0 caused the 2026-07-02 file-page-thrash freeze, see gui_session._comment). These units keep their pages resident in RAM; the rest of the session retains its 6G zram-first valve. Xwayland is spawned as a child of kwin_wayland so it shares kwin's cgroup and inherits swap=0 — no separate unit. Consumed by configuration_system-protection.nix → systemd.user.services.<unit>.serviceConfig.MemorySwapMax.

reservation._comment: THE UNTOUCHABLE ISLAND (user requirement: 'watchdog+mesh MUST HAVE ownership of a never-touched area of disk+memory+cpu to ALWAYS kill whatever overwhelms the system'). Hosts: freeze-guard, earlyoom, sshd, rescue-ssh (connectivity.slice). MemoryMin = guaranteed unreclaimable RAM. CPU = SCHED_FIFO realtime priority preempts ALL normal processes even at 100% load. IO = realtime ioprio class always gets the NVMe queue. OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 = NEVER killed. So the killers + remote rescue can always run, no matter what.

watchdog._comment: freeze-guard: an ACTIVE PSI killer running in the untouchable island. PSI IS THE ONLY KILL METRIC (no absolute CPU%/RSS/mem% triggers — those cause false kills at PSI=0). Every interval_sec it reads /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}: mem/io use 'full avg10' (% of last 10s ALL tasks stalled); cpu uses 'some avg10' (a pure spin stalls some tasks, rarely all). ONLY when a signal exceeds its limit does it act — killing the top offender and re-checking, walking down the rank up to max_kills_per_tick times until pressure drops. Victim RANKING (not trigger) is pressure-aware: CPU breach ranks by %cpu, mem/io breach by RSS; prefer_kill (compilers/browsers) first, then any non-avoid_kill process. Kills are GRACEFUL SIGTERM for node/claude (so Claude Code prints its resume hint), SIGKILL for everything else. Backstop beneath cgroup caps + systemd-oomd. Baked into the service script at build time (reproducible); every action echoed to the journal.
watchdog._write_storm_comment: 2026-07-10 v3.2 — WRITE-STORM voter, the LEADING indicator PSI misses. A big write burst lands in page cache as dirty pages INSTANTLY (no stall → PSI flat); the freeze comes later during writeback when dirty pages exceed vm.dirty_ratio and the kernel forces synchronous writeback (all writes block). By the time io-PSI reflects it you are already frozen. This voter reads /proc/diskstats write rate + /proc/meminfo Dirty+Writeback directly: sustained write rate > write_storm_mb_per_sec for write_storm_sustain_sec, OR dirty backlog > dirty_mb_max, → SIGKILL the top disk WRITER (largest /proc/PID/io write_bytes delta), never a kthread/essential. Catches the storm BEFORE the writeback stall.
watchdog._max_kills_comment: 2026-07-26: raised 4→8. The 14:09 freeze hit memory.events high=2.3 MILLION with the killer sidelined (no eligible victim); 4/tick was already too timid to relieve that scale of thrash even before the eligibility bug. Now data-driven, not hardcoded.
watchdog._hard_protect_comment: 2026-07-26 root cause of the 14:09 freeze: THRASH-KILL logged 'no eligible victim (all avoid_kill?) — cannot act' every tick because the OLD single avoid_kill list was so broad it excluded EVERY candidate inside the throttled slice, so the killer killed nothing and the box froze. hard_protect is now a SHORT, NEVER-KILL CORE tier (init, IPC bus, remote/debug access, the killers themselves, the connectivity/OOM island: systemd-oomd/earlyoom/polkit/NetworkManager/wpa_supplicant — promoted here from soft_avoid because killing the connectivity island or the other OOM daemons is self-defeating). kwin_wayland|plasmashell are DELIBERATELY REMOVED from hard_protect so the fallback victim pool can pick them as an ABSOLUTE LAST RESORT (kill+restart) instead of finding zero eligible victims and freezing; they remain in soft_avoid below so they are never a PREFERRED victim, only a last-resort one when nothing else is left. soft_avoid is the old broad 'prefer not to kill' list, now a PREFERENCE not an absolute veto — pick_cgroup_victim falls back to the largest-RSS soft_avoid process (which can now include the compositor) rather than doing nothing when it's the only candidate left.
watchdog._reset_comment: 2026-07-26 RESET map — some victims are systemd-managed daemons whose death should be a fresh RESTART, not a permanent kill. reset_units matches a victim's comm (grep -E against the map's keys) to the systemd unit to restart after the kill. Classic case: nix-daemon (or a nix build child, e.g. cc1plus/rustc/ld running as its cgroup child under thrash/PSI voters) — SIGKILLing the daemon without restarting it leaves `nix build`/`nix-shell`/home-manager permanently broken until the next boot or manual restart. A non-empty value is a SYSTEM unit restarted via `systemctl restart <unit>`. An empty string means the process is a user-session process that systemd --user / KDE respawns on its own (e.g. kwin_wayland, plasmashell) — still logged as a RESET decision (kill, no explicit restart command) so the journal shows intent, not a plain KILL.
watchdog._thrash_comment: 2026-07-10 v3: the memory.high-THRASH voter — the early detector for the exact failure that PSI missed. The 13:06 freeze had memory.pressure ~35% (below every PSI limit) while user-1000.slice hit memory.high 1.14M times doing reclaim thrash. This voter reads the memory.events 'high' counter delta on thrash_slice each tick; if the per-second rate exceeds high_events_per_sec_max sustained for thrash_sustain_sec, it SIGKILLs the largest-RSS process INSIDE that throttled slice (via cgroup.procs, not systemwide) — the actual runaway, never an innocent. Fires regardless of PSI because it watches the throttle counter itself.
watchdog._perslice_comment: 2026-07-10 v3.1 — THE root cause of the 15:29 freeze: freeze-guard read GLOBAL /proc/pressure/io = 0.14% and never fired, while user.slice io.pressure was 96%/56% (the desktop was IO-STARVED by a bulk writer hogging the NVMe queue). A freeze is a PER-SLICE event; the global gauge is blind to it. These voters read the DESKTOP slice's OWN cgroup pressure files. When the desktop is starved, the fix is to kill the top NON-DESKTOP offender (the hog in workload/machine.slice) — the desktop procs are the victims, not the cause. hog_slices lists where the bulk writers live.
watchdog._kthread_comment: 2026-07-10 v3.1 — the 15:29 guard ran out of real victims and SIGKILLed thermald then tried to kill kworker/R-kthrotld (a KERNEL THREAD, rss=0). Killing a kthread is impossible AND killing essentials makes the freeze worse. kthread_comm_re matches kernel worker comms; any proc matching it, or with rss=0, is NEVER a victim.
watchdog._threshold_evidence: 13:41-13:54 freeze (the third one, during the docker-pull bootstrap): sustained thrash measured at ~2,900 high-events/s (psi-recorder: 1,615,161→1,644,543 in 10s) — BELOW the initial 5000/s guess, so the voter would have sat silent through it. 1000/s is safely under every observed freeze (2900-15000/s) while normal desktop operation idles at <100/s.

watchdog_selfcheck._comment: 2026-07-04 freeze incident root cause: freeze-guard.service was manually stopped (sudo systemctl stop) during debugging at 09:03 and never restarted; the desktop froze 3h22m later with cpuPSI(some)=85%/memPSI(full)=44% (both above freeze-guard's own trigger thresholds) with NO killer running. 'nixos-rebuild switch' does NOT re-arm a manually-stopped-but-unchanged enabled unit — switch-to-configuration only starts/restarts units whose definition changed, so the many switches performed after the manual stop never touched freeze-guard.service (its nix definition was unchanged) and left it stopped indefinitely. This timer is the fix: independent of whether a switch ever runs, periodically verify the PSI killer is active and restart it if not — closes the silent-disarm gap for good.

oomd._comment: systemd-oomd — PSI-aware proactive killer, THE evidence-based fix. The 2026-06-27 forensics (psi-recorder) showed the freezes were user.slice memory.pressure full-avg10 sustained at 62-68% for MINUTES with memory.events oom_kill=0 — the kernel throttled at MemoryHigh and swapped into 20G of swap forever while NOTHING ever killed. enable*Slice turns oomd on for -.slice/system.slice/user.slice, but its built-in default limit is 80% — ABOVE the 65% freeze, so it would never fire. pressure_limit OVERRIDES that to a value below the observed stall so oomd kills the worst cgroup BEFORE the machine locks. PSI is swap-independent, so 20G of swap cannot mask it. duration = sustained-seconds before the kill.
oomd._v3_note: 2026-07-10: pressure_limit 50%→30%, duration 15s→10s. The 13:06 thrash held memory PSI at only ~35-38% — below the old 50% limit — so oomd (correctly, per its config) never fired. 30% sits below the observed thrash band so oomd now kills the worst child cgroup in ~10s. oomd watches memory PSI only; the io-PSI blind spot is covered by freeze-guard's io + thrash voters.

earlyoom._comment: earlyoom — DISABLED 2026-07-03 (user directive: 'remove ALL non-PSI triggers, ONLY PSI'). earlyoom has no PSI flag at all — it is purely absolute free-mem%/free-swap%, and repeatedly killed plasmashell on transient MemAvailable dips while /proc/pressure/memory sat near 0 (reclaim was keeping up fine, no real pressure — first tightened 5/3→2/1 as a partial fix, then fully disabled since ANY absolute threshold can still false-fire at PSI=0). The only two active killers now are systemd-oomd (memory PSI, pressure_limit=50%) and freeze-guard (mem/io/cpu PSI, 40/30/80 full-avg10/full-avg10/some-avg10) — both are genuinely PSI-gated per sysprot.watchdog's own contract ('PSI IS THE ONLY KILL METRIC'). enable=false is the single source of truth (services.earlyoom.enable reads this); flip to true + re-tune thresholds if a non-PSI last-resort backstop is ever wanted again.

sysctl._comment: Writeback + reclaim tuning. Lower dirty ratios flush dirty pages earlier and in smaller batches → no giant NVMe writeback burst that spikes iowait. vfs_cache_pressure<100 keeps dentry/inode cache longer → less metadata IO. min_free_kbytes/watermark keep a kernel reserve so allocation never stalls hard. swappiness 150 = prefer compressed zram over disk (zram is RAM-backed).
sysctl._sysrq_note: 2026-07-10 v3: was the kernel default 16 (sync only) — so Alt+SysRq+F did NOTHING during the freeze. 244 = 4(SAK)+16(sync)+32(remount-ro)+64(signal/OOM-kill: Alt+SysRq+F) +128(reboot/poweroff: Alt+SysRq+B). Arms the physical-keyboard escape hatches: REISUB and manual OOM-kill work even when userspace is fully wedged.

kernel_watchdog._comment: 2026-07-10 v3: last-line kernel escape hatch. The Surface exposes NO hardware watchdog (/sys/class/watchdog empty, RuntimeWatchdogUSec=0) — a true kernel wedge could ONLY be cleared by holding the power button. softdog + systemd's RuntimeWatchdogSec makes PID1 pet /dev/watchdog every runtime_sec/2; if the box is so wedged PID1 can't run, the softdog fires and REBOOTS in runtime_sec. Session-on-disk checkpoints (6h + on-hibernate) bound the blast radius. This is the ONLY mechanism that recovers a hard wedge with no human present — the 'always-on VM' guarantee.

slice_protection._comment: 2026-07-10 v3 IO ladder. Kernel reclaim IO can't be cgroup-weighted, but BULK WRITERS (docker/nix-daemon/backups in workload.slice) can — so they can no longer starve the desktop's own IO the way the 13:06 thrash did. os_essentials ALSO gets a memory reservation: today os-essentials.slice has NO MemoryMin, so reclaim can evict sshd/session/logind pages (the very infra you'd need to debug a freeze). connectivity island already has io_weight=1000 (reservation block); this ladders the rest below it.

testers._comment: Run via the same data-driven runner pattern as test-session-checkpoint.sh. Each check proves one guarantee of the freeze-proof contract.

checks.description: nix-daemon cannot swap (build OOM-kills instead of thrashing the disk)
nix-daemon MemoryMax is the declared hard cap (not the 6G drift value)
user-1000.slice has guaranteed unreclaimable RAM (MemoryMin) so the desktop never freezes
user-1000.slice has a bounded 2G swap valve (zram-first) — not 0 (file-page thrash) and not unlimited (disk thrash)
prochot-guard timer is armed — detects EC BD_PROCHOT hardware clamps (the 200MHz incident class, invisible to PSI)
cpu0 current frequency is at or above the software minimum — no hardware BD_PROCHOT clamp active
the RIGHTCTRL long-press → kernel-OOM escape-hatch watcher is running (untouchable island)
plasma-plasmashell user unit has MemorySwapMax=0 — the compositor can never be paged to swap
plasma-kwin_wayland user unit has MemorySwapMax=0 (Xwayland inherits via kwin's cgroup)
user-1000.slice MemoryHigh is at least 4G — above the measured desktop working set (~3.5G), so no permanent memory.high reclaim throttle
the freeze-guard active PSI killer is running
freeze-guard is general-purpose — its deployed script reacts to CPU pressure, not just mem/io (grep the ExecStart store script; the unit text never contains it)
checks.command: grep -hE 'cpuPSI|psi_avg10' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)" | head -1

checks.description: freeze-guard is in the untouchable island — can never be OOM-killed
freeze-guard runs in the reserved connectivity.slice island

the freeze-guard self-check timer is armed — re-arms the PSI killer within 60s if it's ever manually stopped and left off (2026-07-04 incident: a manual stop at 09:03 survived 3h22m and many nixos-rebuild switches because switch-to-configuration never restarts an unchanged-but-stopped unit)
systemd-oomd PSI killer is running
earlyoom (non-PSI absolute-value killer) is disabled — only PSI-based killers (oomd, freeze-guard) may act
the untouchable island has guaranteed RAM for the killers + mesh
U1: rescue-ssh (Dropbear) listens on the port declared in sysprot.rescue_port (2200), proving rescuePort is read from this JSON not the old hardcoded let-binding

U1: workload.slice CPUQuota = cpus×75% = 8×75 = 600%, proving cpus is derived from sysprot.specs.cpu (=8) not the old hardcoded cpus=8 let-binding (systemd normalizes 600% → CPUQuotaPerSecUSec=6s over a 1s period)

U1: user-0.slice MemoryMax = ramMB×95% = 8192×0.95 = 7782M ≈ 8.16e9 bytes (systemd rounds to page granularity), proving ramMB is derived from sysprot.specs.ram_gb (=8 → 8192MB) not the old hardcoded ramMB=8192 let-binding. Range check tolerates systemd page-alignment rounding.
v3: kernel.sysrq=244 so Alt+SysRq+F (manual OOM) and REISUB work when userspace is wedged (was 16 = sync-only during the 13:06 freeze)
v3: /dev/watchdog exists (softdog loaded) so systemd can pet it and self-reboot a hard wedge (Surface has no HW watchdog)
v3: user-1000.slice (MemoryMax − MemoryHigh) ≤ 536870912 (512M) — no wide 'throttle purgatory' band that reclaim-thrashes forever instead of escalating to a kill (13:06 root cause: 1.2G band)
checks.command: echo $(( $(systemctl show user-1000.slice -p MemoryMax --value) - $(systemctl show user-1000.slice -p MemoryHigh --value) <= 536870912 ))

checks.description: v3: oomd ManagedOOMMemoryPressureLimit = 30% on user.slice — fires at the observed ~35% thrash instead of never (old 50% was above the stall)
v3: os-essentials.slice has a 512M MemoryMin reservation so reclaim can't evict sshd/session/logind pages (the debug infra) — was unreserved
v3: workload.slice IOWeight = 50 — bulk writers (docker/nix/backups) yield the NVMe queue to the desktop + island
v3: freeze-guard's deployed script has the memory.high-thrash voter (memory.events 'high' delta) — the detector for the PSI-invisible reclaim-thrash freeze
checks.command: grep -hE 'HIGH_MAX|memory.events|THRASH' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)" | head -1

checks.description: v3 root-cause fix: freeze-guard escalates an IGNORED SIGTERM to SIGKILL (KILL-ESC) — the 13:06 freeze was the same claude pid SIGTERM'd 20+ times over 75s, never dying, no escalation
checks.command: grep -hc 'KILL-ESC' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)"

checks.description: v3.1 root-cause fix (15:29 freeze): freeze-guard reads the DESKTOP slice's OWN io/memory.pressure (psi_slice_avg10 / DESKTOP-STARVED), not just global /proc/pressure — global was 0.14% while user.slice io was 96%
checks.command: grep -hcE 'psi_slice_avg10|DESKTOP-STARVED' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)"

checks.description: v3.1: freeze-guard never targets kernel threads (is_kthread / KTHREAD_RE) — the 15:29 guard flailed SIGKILLing kworker/thermald when it ran out of real victims
checks.command: grep -hcE 'is_kthread|KTHREAD_RE' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)"

checks.description: v3.2: freeze-guard has the write-storm voter (WRITE-STORM / disk_write_mbps / dirty_mb) — the LEADING indicator PSI misses (a write burst fills dirty cache with no stall, then forces a writeback freeze)
checks.command: grep -hcE 'WRITE-STORM|disk_write_mbps|pick_top_writer' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)"

checks.description: 2026-07-26: freeze-guard's deployed script carries the RESET_UNITS map + do_kill restart logic — victims like nix-daemon get restarted after the kill instead of staying dead
checks.command: grep -hcE 'RESET_UNITS|RESET:' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)"

checks.description: 2026-07-26: root-watchdog has a scoped NOPASSWD sudo rule to restart nix-daemon.service (no more, no less) — the RESET map is otherwise unenforceable since root-watchdog only holds CAP_KILL/CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH
